text:
Predicates:
Adores(max, x) ::: Max adores x.
DesignStyle(x) ::: x is a design style.
ZahaStyle(x) ::: x is Zaha Hadid's design style.
KellyStyle(x) ::: x is Kelly Wearstler's design style.
InterestingGeometry(x) ::: x has interesting geometries.
BrutalistBuilding(x) ::: x is a brutalist building.
Evocative(x) ::: x is evocative.
Dreamy(x) ::: x is dreamy.
Premises:
∀x ((ZahaStyle(x) ∧ Adores(max, x)) → InterestingGeometry(x)) ::: All of Zaha Hadid's design styles that Max adores have interesting geometries.
∀x ((BrutalistBuilding(x) ∧ Adores(max, x)) → ¬InterestingGeometry(x)) ::: No brutalist buildings that Max adores have interesting geometries.
∀x (DesignStyle(x) ∧ Adores(max, x) → (ZahaStyle(x) ∨ KellyStyle(x))) ::: Every style that Max adores is either Zaha Hadid's design style or Kelly Wearstler's design style.
∀x ((KellyStyle(x) ∧ Adores(max, x)) → Evocative(x)) ::: All of Kelly Wearstler's design styles that Max adores are evocative.
∀x ((KellyStyle(x) ∧ Adores(max, x)) → Dreamy(x)) ::: All of Kelly Wearstler's design styles that Max adores are dreamy.
∀x ((Adores(max, x) ∧ InterestingGeometry(x)) → (BrutalistBuilding(x) ∧ Evocative(x))) ::: If a design by Max that he adores has interesting geometries, then the design is a brutalist building and evocative.
Conclusion:
∃x (Adores(max, x) ∧ BrutalistBuilding(x)) ::: A design by Max is a brutalist building.
